sb_prompt: SEE HOW THE OTHER CALLER FEELS ABOUT THE PROPOSAL THAT ALL YOUNG AMERICANS SHOULD SPEND A YEAR OR TWO DOING SOME KIND OF PUBLIC SERVICE
turns: Yeah, I'm actually kind of on the fence about this whole thing myself, honestly.
Yeah, same here. I've been thinking about it for a while but I can't quite figure out why I feel the way I do.
Yeah, I've been thinking about it for years too, but I just can't put my finger on why I'm still kinda doubtful about it.
Yeah, exactly. It feels like everyone else is just jumping on the bandwagon without really looking at it.
It just feels like we're rushing to solve problems that maybe aren't even ours to solve yet.
Yeah, but what about the kids who need that gap year to figure out what they're actually good at?
I mean, I see my own kid wanting to just hang out, but I'm worried it'll just turn into another expensive year doing nothing.
Yeah, but what if that "doing nothing" turns out to be the most important thing they do?
I guess because I'm seeing it more as a job placement delay than actual service.
Yeah, but maybe it's not about finding a job, maybe it's about figuring out what you actually want out of life.
Right, but if they don't have a clue what they want yet, isn't that just a year of them drifting aimlessly with no direction?
But honestly, I think the problem isn't the service, it's that people think it's mandatory.
That's fair, but making it mandatory feels like just another government mandate that nobody actually wants.
Yeah, because nobody signs up for it willingly, it just feels like punishment rather than growth.
Yeah, that's the thing that really bothers me—if it's forced, does it even count as real service anymore?
Yeah, because if you're just forced to shovel snow or sweep floors against your will, it feels less like service and more like community service with an extra 'M' for mandatory.
That makes sense, but if they're doing it just to get it over with, I don't think they'll learn anything real.
Exactly, and honestly, I drive a school bus so I see kids who've already decided their path years ago, so I'm not sure a year of shoveling snow is going to change that for everyone.
I mean, seeing them stuck on the same track for so long makes me think they might just drift anyway no matter what they do.
I guess when you're watching them sit in silence for hours waiting for a bus, you start wondering if any amount of time off is going to fix that stuck feeling.
I guess if the bus driver stuff is just about getting them back on schedule, maybe a year of it won't do anything different for them anyway.
Yeah, but maybe the real fix isn't forcing them into a specific plan, but giving them the time to find their own path without the pressure.
I guess if they're doing it for themselves instead of for the government, maybe that pressure would make it stick.
Yeah, but if it's voluntary, does the government even have the power to enforce it if half the class just skips it?
That's a fair point, but if half the kids just don't show up, isn't it basically just a nice idea that never actually happens?
Yeah, but if nobody shows up, then it's just a nice idea that doesn't actually solve anything for the kids who really need it.
Yeah, but then who pays for the gap for the ones who actually need it most?
Well, that's the thing, if we don't figure out how to pay for it, it's just a dream for the rich kids and nothing for the ones who really need a break.
Yeah, but if the government pays for it, doesn't that just make it another rich kid's vacation for everyone else?
Yeah, but maybe it's not about paying for everyone, just making sure the kids who actually need a break aren't left behind while the rich ones get the whole vacation.
Yeah, but then it's just a nice idea on paper that doesn't actually help anyone.
Yeah, but maybe we shouldn't let it be a paid vacation first, and make it a work camp where everyone pitches in for free, so the rich don't get the perks and the kids actually learn to work together.
Yeah, but if they pitch in for free, how do you keep it from becoming just another unpaid job with no benefits?
Yeah, but maybe we start small and let people choose their own projects, so it doesn't feel like just another unpaid job they're forced to do.
Yeah, but if they choose their own projects, doesn't that just mean they pick the easiest ones and call it service?
Yeah, but maybe if it's a mix of required hours and optional deep dives, they don't have to pick the easy stuff to get it done.
Yeah, but if they mix it up like that, won't the rich ones just pay for the hard stuff while the others do the grunt work and call it service?
Yeah, but maybe we start with a pilot program where only the motivated kids join, and see if that voluntary core actually works before we try to force it on everyone else.
Yeah, but if they just pick what's easy, isn't it still the same old problem just with nicer paperwork?
Yeah, but maybe the hard part isn't the paperwork, it's just getting the first few people actually showing up without it feeling like punishment.
